prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universal “best” — the right HVAC contractor depends on your neighborhood, budget, the size/age of your home, the system you want, and whether you prefer a national brand or a trusted local shop. That said, here’s a practical way to find the best company in Atlanta and some reputable names to consider.

How to choose the best company
- Get at least 3 written estimates that include system make/model, SEER rating, labor, permit costs, and expected timeline.  
- Make sure they will perform a Manual J load calculation (not just “tonnage by rule of thumb”). Correct sizing matters more than brand alone.  
- Check license & insurance: confirm they’re licensed to do HVAC work in Georgia (and carry liability insurance and workers’ comp).  
- Look at recent reviews on Google, BBB, Yelp, and Angi (and ask for local references). Focus on recent installs, not just service calls.  
- Ask about warranties: manufacturer part warranty, compressor warranty, and their workmanship warranty. Get warranty details in writing.  
- Ask about energy-efficiency options and rebates (SEER rating, variable-speed compressors, smart thermostats).  
- Confirm who pulls permits and handles code inspections.  
- Consider financing and maintenance plans if you want predictable costs.

Reputable companies that serve Atlanta (good starting list)
- Coolray Heating & Air Conditioning — large regional company, many installs and service options.  
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (franchised) — nationwide brand with local franchises in Atlanta.  
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (part of the ARS network) — big footprint, often available quickly.  
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning — national chain with warranty/maintenance programs.  
- Aire Serv — franchise network with local operators in Atlanta.  
- Local independent contractors — smaller local companies often get excellent reviews for installation quality and personalized service. Ask neighbors or check Nextdoor for local recommendations.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Will you perform (and provide) a Manual J load calculation?  
- Which exact unit model are you recommending and why? (SEER, tonnage, variable-speed?)  
- What is included in the install (new pad, line set, thermostat, permits, disposal of old unit)?  
- What are the total upfront costs and any available rebates?  
- What warranties are included (manufacturer + labor)? How long and who services the warranty?  
- Do you offer maintenance plans and financing?

Typical efficiency guidance for Atlanta
- Look for at least 16 SEER for good efficiency in Atlanta’s climate; 14 SEER is minimum allowed in many new install contexts but higher SEER saves energy. Consider variable-speed equipment if noise and humidity control are priorities.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow the list to top-rated contractors near your ZIP code,  
- Help you draft an RFP/email to send to contractors to get comparable bids, or  
- Review estimates you receive and point out red flags.

Tell me your ZIP code, house size/age, and whether you have brand preferences or a target budget and I’ll give more specific recommendations.
